predictions.why: Under the mixture mechanism the plain prompt leaves about 10-15 % of top8 samples (~65 answers, ~half wrong) in the plain-base register; the cue moves those into the cued/RL-like register (~85-93 % right), adding ~25 right to top8 plain's 427, in line with the theta line where the cue adds +36 at a=0.25 (405->441) and +9 at a=0.5 (443->452).

intervention.change: Selection only, no new generation: majority vote over the 4 stored Day-1 #3 cued-base samples (attempt 0) in which finished answers with n_new <= 600 tokens (the plain-register signature: short, quick answers) are dropped from the vote unless every sample of the problem is that short; cap hits never vote; ties go to the lowest sample index.

cell.prompt: plain MATH prompt + prefilled cue ids [1584, 2268, 33413] (" line!\n\nOkay")
cell.seeds: seed base 41,000,000 + problem index + 10,000*sample (stored rows of studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl, attempt 0)

intervention.count: Problems of 500 whose voted extracted_v3 answer is right under grader v3 (a problem whose samples all hit the cap or give no answer counts wrong); computed from rows.jsonl attempt-0 rows using n_new, cap_hit, extracted_v3 and score_v3.

best_known.setting: cue, T 1.0, vote over 4 stored samples, ties to the shortest finished sample (rule chosen on this set; held-out 451)

intervention.why: The mechanism puts quick wrong answers in a short plain-base register that is wrong about half the time regardless of difficulty, so removing those votes should let the deliberative samples decide; since the cue already switches most cued-base samples, few are that short and the gain over the plain 446 vote is at most a few problems.
